items.title: 'It's Good to Be Back': Johnny Depp Meets Fans as Ebenezer Scrooge, as First Trailer Drops for His Big Hollywood Return
items.description: Johnny Depp has returned to the Hollywood limelight with a surprise appearance at Comic-Con in character as Ebenezer Scrooge.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Johnny Depp has returned to the Hollywood limelight with a surprise appearance at Comic-Con in character as Ebenezer Scrooge.

The Pirates of the Caribbean and Edward Scissorhands star greeted fans in full costume and makeup as the Dickensian antihero, who he'll play in this year's star-studded Christmas movie Ebenezer — a project widely seen as Depp's big Hollywood comeback.

Ebenezer will also feature Ian McKellen, Daisy Ridley, Rupert Grint, Andrea Riseborough and Tramell Tillman in a new twist on the beloved Christmas tale, though all eyes will be on Depp in its starring role — his first major Hollywood part in nearly a decade, following the widely-publicized legal troubles with ex-wife Amber Heard.

This week has seen fans given their best look yet at Depp as Scrooge, via a new trailer (above) and a couple of in-person appearances at San Diego Comic-Con. Depp appeared at a pop-up recreation of his house, chatting away with onlookers and eventually dropping the character's signature catchphrase of "humbug" to cheers (you can see this in the video below). The actor then popped up unexpectedly during the event's Directors on Directing panel to reveal Ebenezer's trailer to the audience.

After years focusing on smaller projects and international films, the path now seems to be opening up for Depp to make a career comeback — though a question mark still hangs over whether he will ever resume his most iconic role: Pirates of the Caribbean's Captain Jack Sparrow.

Disney has long had plans to continue its buccaneer movie franchise, and producer Jerry Bruckheimer has talked positively of wanting Depp back. Speaking last year, Bruckheimer confirmed "some" previous Pirates of the Caribbean actors would return for the next movie, while offering "a new take" on the franchise overall.

Whether this actually happens, however, remains to be seen — though a positive response to Ebenezer when it arrives this November 13 may change that.

Image credit: Daniel Knighton/Getty Images for Paramount Pictures

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

items.title: PlayStation Killing Discs Has Upsides, Ubisoft Boss Yves Guillemot Says, Pointing to Cheaper Consoles Without Disc Drives
items.description: Sony's controversial decision to kill PlayStation 5 discs could have some upsides, Ubisoft boss Yves Guillemot has said.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Sony's controversial decision to kill PlayStation 5 discs could have some upsides, Ubisoft boss Yves Guillemot has said.

Speaking yesterday during the company's most recent investor Q&A, Guillemot was asked by an analyst for his thoughts on Sony's bombshell announcement that it would discontinue discs for new PS5 games from January 2028 onwards, announced earlier this month.

Perhaps predictably, Guillemot did not strike too downbeat a tone in his answer — in contrast to the huge wave of negative backlash from fans that has been seen online, across social media, livestream comments and an enormous petition. Indeed, Guillemot suggested that some positives would come from the move.

"What we saw on the PC is that it helped to grow the market," Guillemot noted. "There's also some pressure for the future on the cost of machines and being able to be only digital will help to have a more accessible machine, I would say."

Ultimately, Guillemot concluded that Sony's decision would likely not impact the wider industry too much — regardless of the passionate response by actual gamers, which Sony is seemingly doing its best job right now of ignoring.

"There are plus and minus," the Ubisoft CEO concluded, "but we think it will not disturb too much the industry."

Guillemot's comments reflect the fact that the vast majority of game purchases are already digital, following the rise of downloads over the past decade. Indeed, Sony's rationale for ditching discs is that it's simply following consumer trends. "In response to shifting trends in consumer preference, new games will be released on PlayStation Store and at retailers in digital formats only," Sid Shuman, Senior Director, Sony Interactive Entertainment Content Communications, said in a post on PlayStation Blog, effectively telling gamers that this outcome was in a response to their own spending habits.

"As consumer preferences and the broader entertainment industry continue to shift away from physical discs to digital, physical game disc production for all new games releasing on PlayStation consoles will be discontinued starting January 2028. Following this date, new games will be available on PlayStation Store and at retailers in digital formats only. This transition has no impact on games that already released, or will be releasing, prior to January 2028 in disc format.

"This is a natural direction for Sony Interactive Entertainment to adapt to consumer trends as the general preference for digital media significantly outpaces physical discs. This transition will enable us to align more closely with how most of our community prefers to access and play games today."

Still, the online blowback to Sony's announcement has been huge, with the most vocal proponents of physical releases leading the charge, citing concerns over game ownership and preservation among the key issues. This week, a former God of War developer revealed that Sony knew its decision to kill PlayStation 5 discs would spark outrage, and reportedly issued staff with the "strictest" social media guidelines to stop them from publicly commenting on the controversy.

But Sony seems unlikely to change course, and it has already begun reassigning staff involved with disc production. Cruically, Sony simply earns more money from digital games — at a time when consoles sales are being impacted by rising costs. For a first-party PlayStation game such as The Last of Us, Sony will only keep around 65% of the money from a physical copy, with around 30% going to the retailer and roughly another 5% on manufacturing costs. Meanwhile, for a physical copy of a third-party game such as the Activision-published Call of Duty, Sony will get a licensing fee, likely around 15%. For digital sales, Sony keeps 100% of first-party game revenue, and a far better cut from third-party titles.

Like it or not — and many won't — financially it's hard to argue with Guillemot's assessment, even if it will likely only stir up more frustration among fans. Speaking to IGN, analysts have all said similar. Dr. Serkan Toto, CEO of Japanese game industry consultancy firm Kantan Games, suggested that even if half a million people cancelled their PlayStation Plus subscription in protest, it would be just a drop in the ocean for Sony.

"I sympathize with physical media fans, but Sony will not reverse this decision," Toto told IGN. "They of course knew what the online reaction would look like, and they now wait for this storm to pass.

"Sony has over 120 million active PlayStation users," he continued. "Around 50 million people subscribe to PlayStation Plus. As a thought experiment, let's say 500,000 cancel in protest, that would be just 1% of that business gone — of course not enough for Sony to start rethinking. Digital is just too lucrative."

Image credit: Nathan Laine/Bloomberg via Getty Images.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

items.title: 'One Day, I'm Sure': Spider-Man: Brand New Day Star Tom Holland Teases Venom Symbiote
items.description: Tom Holland has teased a return of the Venom Symbiote, as the hours count down to the launch of Spider-Man: Brand New Day.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Tom Holland has teased a return of the Venom Symbiote, as the hours count down to the launch of Spider-Man: Brand New Day.

Asked by a young fan if Holland's Spider-Man would ever encounter the Symbiote, Holland said he couldn't answer the question directly — but added that the moment would come "one day, I'm sure."

"We'll get to see the Symbiote," Holland continued, in a moment posted to Instagram by cinempolismx.

Could the Symbiote appear in Brand New Day? It's a question that fans have been debating ever since the movie's first trailer showed Holland's webslinger emerging from a sticky cocoon, with mention that he was undergoing some form of transformation.

Remember, of course, that Spider-Man: No Way Home concluded with a brief shot of the Symbiote — or a part of it — being left behind in the MCU following that film's various multiversal shenanigans. The possibility is certainly there for more from the Symbiote, and many fans see Holland donning a black Symbiote suit as inevitable before he ends his run.

With Brand New Day already stuffed full of foes, the only question seems to be when the Symbiote storyline will be adapted. Could Holland be infected at the end of Brand New Day, with the transformation happening off-screen — potentially explaining his absence in this year's Avengers: Doomsday? That could leave him ready and powered-up to make a triumphant return in 2027's Avengers: Secret Wars.

Alternatively, the widely-expected future films in Holland's second trilogy of Spider-Man movies could center on the Symbiote — perhaps changing Peter Parker's personality just as his identity is restored in the memories of best pal Ned and ex-girlfriend MJ. Let's just hope this incarnation of Peter Parker leaves the dance moves at home, though.

With previews early next week and its official July 31 release date fast approaching, Holland is currently in the middle of a whirlwind Spider-Man: Brand New Day press tour, and proving as chatty as ever. Yesterday, Holland raised eyebrows by flatly denying Jean Grey was in the movie — despite huge speculation that this is who Sadie Sink is playing. The actor has also teased that the movie's title will be explained in its final frame (intriguing!), revealed that "one person" still remembers Peter Parker is Spider-Man (Sadie Sink?) and discussing his potential involvement in the upcoming Avengers movies — which he strongly suggested he will feature in.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

items.title: Seth Green’s Star Wars: Detours Will Finally See the Light of Day
items.description: A selection of episodes from Seth Green’s animated Star Wars sitcom will be exhibited at the soon-to-open Lucas Museum.
items.author: Luke Reilly
items.content:
Seth Green’s long-shelved animated Star Wars sitcom Star Wars: Detours will finally find itself in front of the public, albeit as an exhibit at George Lucas’ soon-to-open Lucas Museum of Narrative Art in Los Angeles, California. The news comes via an announcement from Green himself during a panel discussion on the museum at San Diego Comic-Con 2026, as reported by Entertainment Weekly.

“We made a show with George, an animated series,” said Green. “He wanted to make Simpsons in the Star Wars universe. It’s called Detours, and there’s… going to be a curation of episodes from that show on display for the public in the theater.”

Star Wars Detours was officially announced way back at Star Wars Celebration in 2012, although Lucas and Green were broadly discussing the project in public as early as 2010. A variety of clips were showcased around its 2012 reveal, but the series was shelved in the aftermath of Disney’s acquisition of Lucasfilm the same year and its been missing in action ever since.

Green discussed the status of Star Wars Detours with IGN in late 2013 at New York Comic-Con, confirming the crew had 39 episodes completed before the show was frozen in carbonite.

The Lucas Museum of Narrative Art is set to open on September 22. Two theaters (the Robert Flaherty Theater and the Slavko Vorkapich Theater) will showcase curated film selections throughout the day for patrons to drop in and drop out of during their visit.

Luke is a Senior Editor on the IGN reviews team. You can track him down on Bluesky @mrlukereilly to ask him things about stuff.

items.title: 'It's Being Written, Is the Short Answer' — Zach Cregger Gives an Update on the Aunt Gladys Prequel | Comic Con 2026
items.description: Director Zach Cregger said that the Aunt Gladys-focused Weapons prequel movie is in the works and will have "lots of twists and turns and mysteries and crazy things" at San Diego Comic-Con.
items.author: Leanne Butkovic
items.content:
Weapons and upcoming Resident Evil director Zach Cregger gave an update on the status of his Aunt Gladys prequel film at San Diego Comic-Con on Thursday afternoon.

"First of all, I'm really excited about the Gladys movie. I loved working with Amy [Madigan], I love that character," Cregger said. "For the movie Weapons, it really made a lot of sense not to dive into her backstory because the device of Weapons was to keep her very opaque and very mysterious. However, I think there's an amazing story to be told about where Gladys comes from and how she became what we know her as. It's got a lot of twists and turns and mysteries and crazy things, kind of like Weapons does, and I think it's gonna be great. The script is in process now and we're taking it very seriously and it's moving in the right direction. It's being written, is the short answer."

An appetite for an Aunt Gladys prequel film gained traction barely a week after Weapons first came out in August 2025. The writer and director confirmed in September 2025 that the development talks with Warner Bros., which distributed Weapons, were "not bullshit." In April 2026 — not long after Madigan won Best Supporting Actress for her performance as Gladys at the Oscars — the trades reported that Zach Shields (Godzilla: King of the Monsters), would be joining Cregger as co-writer on the script. The working title is currently, simply, Gladys.

Despite the active work on the Weapons prequel, Cregger said that it will not be his next film — that will be sci-fi thriller The Flood, produced by Steven Spielberg's Amblin Entertainment, which already has a release date slated for August 11, 2028. Gladys will come after that. Meanwhile, he's also producing a Siren Head film in the creepypasta horror space.

The Resident Evil director shared the panel stage with directors Jonathan Goldstein and John Francis Daley — who shared directing duties on Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves and Game Night, and are helming Apple TV's upcoming Mayday, starring Ryan Reynolds and Kenneth Branaugh.

Speaking of Resident Evil, the director talked about his all-out approach in telling a "straightforward" story. "I wanted to see if I could put my foot all the way down on the gas pedal and not let up until the end of the movie," he said. "That was the challenge: Can I just be completely unrelenting? You guys will tell me if that's the case."

Cregger will be passing through IGN's studio at Comic-Con, along with Resident Evil star Austin Abrams, to talk about the upcoming film, which premieres September 18. Fans were stoked to learn a few weeks ago that the runtime would barely crack 90 minutes.

Leanne Butkovic (she/they) is an Editorial Project Manager at IGN, where they've also written about TV, movies, and games.

items.title: 'Everything Leaks' — Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender Director Addresses Early Concept Photo Leaks | Comic Con 2026
items.description: All the big announcements out of the Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender panel at San Diego Comic-Con 2026.
items.author: Leanne Butkovic
items.content:
While showing off an early concept photo of the aged-up Team Avatar at a San Diego Comic-Con panel on Thursday afternoon, Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender director Lauren Montgomery recalled one of the films' earliest leaks in a rollout that's been plagued by unfortunate leaks. The image in question was what Montgomery called the "Avengers shot," with the characters posing together that leaked out of CinemaCon in 2024 before it was taken down.

"This was one of the very first funny stories about this image. We had a version of this image, exact same painting. The characters looked a little bit different," Montgomery said. "Our production designer Jake [Panian] was never really happy with it. And then Paramount comes to us and says, ‘We want to go to CinemaCon.’ Jake is, like, ‘Absolutely not. It's gonna leak.’ They're like, ‘No, no, no, no. It won't leak. Everything's safe.’ Everything leaks. [Jake]'s like, 'Well, if they're gonna leak it, I'm gonna repaint the whole thing.' And he did. And it looks beautiful, and it looks amazing, and we've used this image a lot of times. And of course, it leaked. Cell phone camera footage of it from a weird angle. And then it's used as, like, official artwork in freakin’ interviews and posts everywhere. So, good time."

Moving on from the anecdote, Montgomery walked through a slideshow of early character design concept art. She showed an Aang with a chinstrap-style beard, many iterations of Zuko's hairstyle, multiple versions of Sokka ("The note was alsays don’t let 'Sokka get TOO hot,'" Montgomery said), Toph in a "metalbending police get-up," and a pregnant Katara. "We moved away from that for our own reasons but a lot of those versions influenced the final version of Katara we see in the film," Montgomery said.

"We're trying to keep this art form alive a little bit longer.”

In mapping out how the team would then animate these rendered images for the feature film, Avatar co-creator Bryan Konietzko reflected on maintaining the importance of Avatar's defining animation style in the same panel that was attended by his fellow Avatar creator Mike DiMartino and most of the core voice cast of the movie. “One of the first things that we talked about was what the medium was going to be. No one told us, but we just assumed: It's a feature film. There's incredible stuff, like Spider-Verse, Arcane… people are doing really stylized, beautiful things with 3D characters that are kind of pushed more towards to 3D. So we just assumed initially, 'Oh, I guess that's what we'll do.’ And we started trying to figure out what that would look like.

"But then one day it just hit me," Konietzko continued. "I was like, ‘What are we doing? This is Avatar. This is a love letter to Japanese anime. This needs to stay 2D. These characters need to be hand drawn.’

Our friends and peers in the industry — in the Western industry, especially — they want to do 2D, but they're being forced to do 3D. And again, there's beautiful stuff being done in 3D, but as artists, we should be able to explore all these different mediums. Mike and I were just like, 'You know what? We're gonna do 2D,' and luckily, our bosses were not forcing us to do 3D. So that's what we did. We're trying to keep this art form alive a little bit longer.”

Creating a New Langauge System

Konietzko also walked through the process of creating a new written language for the universe moving forward, called Avatarian.

A look at the written language!#SDCC2026 #ATLA #AvatarAang pic.twitter.com/AtkpZyt8h8

— Cartoon Universe (@CartoonUV) July 23, 2026

“When we came back to do Avatar studios, we were working with our cultural consultants," Konietzko said. "Now that we had more time and resources for some projects, we had some discussions and realized doing the traditional thing we've been doing, where we're using Chinese as the rhythm language for the Avatar world. That was great, and we love that stuff, but it didn't make as much sense with all the kind of real-world cultures that we pull from for inspiration in Avatar. So I was like, ‘All right, I'm going to create a written language for Avatar.’  

"So I just locked myself in my office for like three months. But I never like in fantasy stuff when the fantasy language just looks like English in cosplay, you know? It just looks like the Roman alphabet in cosplay. items.title: House of the Dragon Larys Strong Actor Matthew Needham Voices Joker in Batman: Caped Crusader Season 2 | Comic Con 2026
items.description: Matthew Needham is the voice of The Joker in Batman: Caped Crusader Season 2, Prime Video has announced. British actor Needham is most famous for playing Larys Strong in Game of Thrones prequel series House of the Dragon.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Matthew Needham is the voice of The Joker in Batman: Caped Crusader Season 2, Prime Video has announced. British actor Needham is most famous for playing Larys Strong in Game of Thrones prequel series House of the Dragon.

Confirmation comes from the Batman: Caped Crusader Season 2 panel at San Diego Comic-Con, which ended with a trailer for Amazon’s upcoming Batman: Caped Crusader - Chronicles game. It’s exclusive to Amazon Luna (and now, part of Amazon Prime), and launches alongside all 10 episodes of Season 2 on July 31.

Batman: Caped Crusader is a superhero noir animated series created by Bruce Timm (co-creator of Batman: The Animated Series), The Batman director Matt Reeves, and J.J. Abrams. The show follows a rookie, early-career Bruce Wayne as he takes on Gotham's criminal underworld in a 1940s setting.

Here’s the official blurb from Prime Video:

Batman: Caped Crusader is a hard-boiled animated series that follows the fearsome vigilante in his early years. Forged in the fire of tragedy, billionaire Bruce Wayne becomes something both more and less than human — the Batman. Night after night, against overwhelming odds, he wages his relentless one-man war on crime.
The series is a reimagining of the Batman mythology through the visionary lens of executive producers J.J. Abrams, Matt Reeves and Bruce Timm. Based on DC characters, Batman: Caped Crusader hails from Warner Bros. Animation, DC Studios, Abrams’ Bad Robot Productions and Reeves’ 6th & Idaho. Along with Abrams, Reeves and Timm, Batman: Caped Crusader executive producers include James Tucker, Geoffrey Thorne, Sarah Geismer, Rachel Rusch Rich, and Sam Register.

Batman: Caped Crusader Season 2 voice cast

Returning voice cast members for Season 2 include Hamish Linklater as Bruce Wayne/Batman, Jamie Chung as Harley Quinn/Harleen Quinzel, Jason Watkins as Alfred Pennyworth, Eric Morgan Stuart as Commissioner Jim Gordon, Krystal Joy Brown as Barbara Gordon, Michelle C. Bonilla as Renee Montoya, and Bumper Robinson as Lucius Fox.

IGN’s Batman: Caped Crusader Season 1 review returned a 7/10. We said: “Batman: Caped Crusader isn’t Batman: The Animated Series, but it does apply its spirit to a captivating detective story.”

items.title: Amazon Prime Has an Exclusive Batman Video Game Set to Launch Alongside Batman: Caped Crusader Season 2 | Comic Con 2026
items.description: Amazon and Warner Bros. have announced Batman: Caped Crusader - Chronicles, a new Batman game exclusive to Amazon Prime set to launch on July 31 alongside Batman: Caped Crusader Season 2.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Amazon and Warner Bros. have announced Batman: Caped Crusader - Chronicles, a new Batman game exclusive to Amazon Prime set to launch on July 31 alongside Batman: Caped Crusader Season 2.

Both the game and the new season of the animated show will be available for Amazon Prime members at no additional cost. The game is part of Amazon Luna’s move into Prime Video, which launched today ahead of the Batman: Caped Crusader Season 2 panel at San Diego Comic-Con.

Batman: Caped Crusader - Chronicles is a cooperative crime-solving party game for up to four players. The idea is that people will watch Batman: Caped Crusader Season 2 then play the game, using their phones as controllers.

Here’s the official blurb:

As a crew of detectives, you’ll step into the dark, noir-soaked streets of Gotham City to become part of a special GCPD task force and Batman’s inner circle. Alongside Detective Montoya, you’ll interrogate, investigate, and deduce your way through 11 episodic missions, each featuring a distinct sleuthing minigame that tests your detective skills. Working together, you’ll foil Batman’s Rogues Gallery of villains, including Babyface, Scarecrow, Dollmaker, and even The Joker.

The game features Hamish Linklater as Batman and Michelle C. Bonilla as Detective Montoya, reprising their roles from the series. Additional voice talent will be announced ahead of the game's July 31 launch.

Batman: Caped Crusader - Chronicles isn’t necessarily the Batman video game core fans are desperate for, but it’s clearly aimed at a more casual gaming audience. Rocksteady, making of the much-loved Batman Arkham video games, is reportedly working on another single-player Batman game in the wake of the failure of live-service game Suicide Squad: Kill the Justice League.

On July 31, Batman: Caped Crusader - Chronicles will be available to Prime members and Luna subscribers on the Luna app in the U.S., UK, Canada, Germany, France, Italy, Spain, Austria, the Netherlands, Poland, Sweden, Portugal, Belgium, and Luxembourg.

At the same San Diego Comic-Con panel, Prime Video announced the voice actor behind Joker in Season 2 of Batman: Caped Crusader.

items.title: After the Avengers Fall, Marvel Will Introduce the Maximum X-Men | Comic Con 2026
items.description: With Avengers: Armageddon decimating Earth's Mightiest Heroes, a new team of mutant heroes will rise up to fil lthe void in Marvel's Maximum X-Men.
items.author: Jesse Schedeen
items.content:
Marvel Comics continues to tease a major shake-up for the Avengers franchise thanks to Avengers: Armageddon, a series that is said to be as important to Earth's Mightiest Heroes as 2004's Avengers: Disassembled. This new series will leave the Avengers broken and reeling, but the world will still need heroes. And it seems the X-Men are being tapped to fill that void.

During their Avengers: Armageddon panel at SDCC 2026 today, Marvel revealed a new ongoing series called Maximum X-Men. Spinning out of the events of Armageddon, Maximum X-Men sees Storm spearhead a new team that includes Wolverine, Colossus, Bishop, Iceman, Psylocke, Firestar, and Justice. Their goal is to defend the globe and fill the void left by the Avengers.

Maximum X-Men is written by Chris Yost (X-Force) and drawn by Tony Daniel (X-Men). Here's the official description of the new series:

In the wake of the events of Avengers: Armageddon, Earth’s Mightiest Heroes are no more! So who will stand in defense of the Earth? The X-Men will! Storm gathers an elite team for just that task, including Wolverine, Colossus, Bishop, Iceman, Psylocke, Firestar and Justice! Mutants by birth, heroes by choice! And their first challenge is a full-on invasion from the Negative Zone! Is this Annihilus again—or something far, far worse?

Maximum X-Men #1 will be released in December 2026.

Also during the panel, Marvel revealed new cover art and details for several Avengers-centric titles releasing this fall. Most intriguingly, we saw a new teaser drawn by Avengers artist Chip Zdarsky that teases a big role for The Punisher in the second arc of that upcoming series. We also learned that Joshua Williamson's Iron Man will start double-shipping in December as it kicks off parallel storylines called "Incarcerated Iron Man" and "War Machines." You can see all the new art revealed in the slideshow gallery below:

In other Comic-Con news, Oni Press revealed the first new Scott Pilgrim comic in 16 years, and we got an exclusive first look at Hasbro's The Legend of Zelda figures.

items.title: Avatar: Seven Havens Gets Paramount+ Release Date and Teaser Trailer | Comic Con 2026
items.description: Avatar: Seven Havens launches exclusively on Paramount+ on October 9. Paramount announced the release date alongside a teaser trailer at the Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender panel at San Diego Comic-Con 2026 today.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Avatar: Seven Havens launches exclusively on Paramount+ on October 9. Paramount announced the release date alongside a teaser trailer at the Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender panel at San Diego Comic-Con 2026 today.

Seven Havens is the new, 26-episode 2D-animated series from Avatar creators Michael DiMartino and Bryan Konietzko. It revolves around a young Earthbender who discovers she’s the new Avatar after Korra in a world shattered by a devastating cataclysm. In this dangerous era, that title marks her as humanity's destroyer, not its savior. Hunted by both human and spirit enemies, she and her long-lost twin must uncover their mysterious origins and save the Seven Havens before civilization’s last strongholds collapse.

New Legends Will Rise. Avatar: Seven Havens, coming to Paramount+ Oct 9th pic.twitter.com/oKc3zXiLNn

— Paramount+ (@paramountplus) July 23, 2026

At SDCC last year, Konietzko said this Earthbender was called Pavi, and introduced her cat monkey, Geet, and her mentor Jae, who is an Airbender. They live in a city called Allura.

Avatar: Seven Havens cast and characters

  • Saheli Khan as Pavi
  • Aishu Devan as Nisha
  • Akshay Khanna as Karthik
  • Major Curda as Jae
  • Sakina Jaffrey as Agam
  • Darren Barnet as Daemin
  • Dianne Doan as Zi
  • Dee Bradley Baker as Geet and Ruhi

Konietzko described Avatar: Seven Havens as "something totally different." "We like to change up the style," he continued. "We like to make each project its own thing. As you can see, it still feels like Avatar, but the world is very different. You'll have to tune in to find out why."

The Avatar: Seven Havens news comes just days before Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender — once due out in theaters on October 9 — hits Paramount+.

Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

items.title: Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls Reveals First Year 1 DLC Character, Opening Movie Released | Comic Con 2026
items.description: Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls has revealed its first Year 1 DLC character alongside its opening movie during a panel at San Diego Comic-Con 2026.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls has revealed its first Year 1 DLC character alongside its opening movie during a panel at San Diego Comic-Con 2026.

The first DLC character for the upcoming 4v4 tag team fighting game is Phoenix Cyclops, voiced by Ray Chase. Chase voices Cyclops in Disney+ show X-Men '97 and hero shooter Marvel Rivals. The DLC character is inspired by his Phoenix Five incarnation from Avengers vs. X-Men, and uses the power of the Phoenix Force, made famous by fellow X-Men mutant, Jean Grey. Phoenix Cyclops is due out fall 2026 as the first of four DLC characters and one new stage coming during the game's first year.

"Unleash devastating Optic Blasts, relentless close-range pressure, and the cosmic flames of the Phoenix Force," Arc System Works said of Phoenix Cyclops' fighting style.

Meanwhile, we have the Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls opening movie below. Developer Arc System Works said the opening movie was inspired by classic fighting games and early 2000s anime openings. It was made by Japanese animation studio Sanzigen, under the direction of Daisuke Suzuki.

The song in the opening movie is called Stronger as One, and will be available on streaming platforms from 9pm PST tonight.

Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls launches on PC and PlayStation 5 on August 6.

items.title: The Steam Deck's Demand Has Reportedly Cratered
items.author: Jacqueline Thomas
items.content:
For years, the Steam Deck was essentially a budget all-star among handheld gaming PCs, even when more powerful handhelds like the Xbox Ally X started coming out. But, in the months following Valve's price increase for its handheld, it seems like demand for the Steam Deck has absolutely cratered.

Right now, it looks like the Steam Deck is selling up to 82% fewer units than it did last year, according to some napkin math done by Boiling Steam (via Gizmodo). The blog is based on the Steam Deck slipping from a near-constant 5th-place on the Steam top sellers chart down to around #14, which is theoretically a massive 72% drop in revenue.

Obviously, these aren't official numbers, and it's unlikely that Valve will ever actually share exactly how many Steam Decks its selling these days. Either way, though, it's not exactly surprising that the Steam Deck isn't moving as fast as it used to. At its new price of $789, the Steam Deck is straight up a worse deal than some of its competitors like the Xbox Ally or the Lenovo Legion Go S – unless you're really attached to the Deck's haptic trackpads.

However, there is a chance that the Steam Deck may grow more popular again. Valve is far from the only company raising prices on its handhelds, and if devices like the white Xbox Ally go up in price, the Steam Deck will start being competitive again. Then again, there's going to be some amount of people that won't be able to afford Valve's prices even if there aren't any cheaper options.

One thing that's for sure, though, is that prices aren't going to improve soon. Valve itself came out and said that retail prices are lagging behind supplier prices by a few months, and the Xbox Series X just got another price increase, scheduled for August. And with Microsoft suggesting that prices for memory are going to end up being five times what they once were, there are almost definitely more price increases right around the corner.

Jackie Thomas is the Hardware and Buying Guides Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

items.title: Supergirl Sets Digital Release Date After Disappointing Run in Theaters
items.description: Supergirl debuts in North America on Digital on July 28, after a disappointing run in theaters that saw just $121 million made at the global box office.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Supergirl debuts in North America on Digital on July 28, after a disappointing run in theaters that saw just $121 million made at the global box office.

On July 28, Supergirl will be available at home on participating digital platforms, including Amazon Prime Video, Apple TV, Fandango, and more. The DC Universe movie then launches on 4K UHD, Blu-ray, and DVD on September 8.

Supergirl, which stars Milly Alcock in the dual role of Supergirl/Kara Zor-El, followed last year’s DCU kickstarter Superman, but failed to generate anywhere near as much interest from cinemagoers. It was deemed a box office bomb when it debuted to a global total of $68 million following its June 26 premiere. The Warner Bros. superhero movie reportedly had a $170 million production budget and $120 million marketing budget, suggesting the studio would need around $300 million just to break even. Supergirl didn’t come close to that milestone.

"While Supergirl didn’t meet our box office expectations," DC Studios co-CEO Peter Safran told The New York Times following Supergirl's opening weekend, "it’s just one component of a broader, long-term strategy at DC Studios that we remain confident in."

To that end, Lanterns is set to premiere on HBO Max in August, Clayface comes out in October, then Superman follow-up Man of Tomorrow hits theaters in 2027.

Alcock will play a significant role in Man of Tomorrow and beyond, DC Studios has said. Supergirl takes place after the events of Superman and sees her encounter other galactic characters like Lobo, played by Jason Momoa. As for Man of Tomorrow, all we really know about the movie is that Superman and supervillain Lex Luthor have to work together to combat the threat of Brainiac. But we can also expect to see the main cast from Superman return. With Supergirl’s involvement, could we see the Justice League finally take shape?

For more, you can check out IGN's 6/10 Supergirl review. You can also read about some behind-the-scenes details that suggest creative differences between DC Studios co-CEO James Gunn and director Craig Gillespie impacted the final product.

Supergirl Digital, 4K UHD, and Blu-ray contain over 90 minutes of bonus features including the following:

  • The Making of Supergirl Consider Supergirl a “Hero’s Journey” for Milly Alcock. She transformed throughout the process of leading her first feature film. We watch as a fly-on-the-wall during key moments of production.
  • Flying Off the Page Supergirl: Woman of Tomorrow, written by Tom King with art by Bilquis Evely, was the jumping off point for DC to adapt Supergirl into a film. We follow the comic authors, screenwriter Ana Nogueira, and filmmakers, as they make the leap from page to screen.
  • Space is a Bad Neighborhood, Babe Explore with Production Designer Neil Lamont, as he takes us through the many worlds that Kara Zor-El steps into on her journey to hunt down Krem of the Yellow Hills.
  • A Practical Legacy There are so many aliens and unique looks in this film that are literally out of this world! Legacy Effects and Peter Swords King explain the creative process behind this diverse group of creatures.
  • Showdown at Evely Square Production spent a month filming this action set-piece. From stunt training, to crashing tanks, to classic superhero flying moments, this breaks down the making of an incredible action scene.
  • The DC Dream: Lobo Jason Momoa has been outspoken over wanting to play Lobo for years, and now his time has come. Go behind the scenes as he transforms into this iconic and chaotic character.
  • Mixtape for a Hero What does Supergirl, as a character, sound like? Director Craig Gillespie and Composer Claudia Sarne answer this question as they discuss the score for the film.
  • You Are Here: A Supergirl Map of the Galaxy If you want to know more about all the planets visited in the film, check out this piece, narrated by Ruthye herself, actress Eve Ridley, to learn some more details, and enjoy the alien aesthetic of the film up close!
  • Girl's Best Friend Krypto is Kara’s badly-behaved BFF and last connection to her home world of Krypton. We delve into their relationship and what makes it so special.
  • Krypto Saves the Day: Coastal Catastrophe An animated short that tells the story of a fun day at the beach which goes sideways when some sneaky foes get between Krypto and his hot dog.
  • Deleted Scenes

items.title: Disgaea Creator Slams Sony for Scrapping Discs, Says PlayStation Might as Well 'Go All the Way' and Scrap Consoles Too
items.description: Disgaea creator and former Nippon Ichi Software CEO Sohei Niikawa has criticized Sony’s decision to ditch physical games, and said that the executives responsible didn't "understand the feelings" of impacted fans.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Disgaea creator and former Nippon Ichi Software CEO Sohei Niikawa has criticized Sony’s decision to ditch physical games, and said that the executives responsible didn't "understand the feelings" of impacted fans.

Earlier this month, Sony announced that from January 2028 onwards it will no longer produce disc releases of new games. This decision triggered huge backlash online, with fans even expressing their anger at Sony in the comments on trailers for unrelated upcoming third party games.

Noisy Pixel interviewed Niikawa at Anime Expo 2026, where he was promoting his upcoming game, Demons’ Night Fever, which describes itself as a speedrun-training simulation RPG. He also gave his opinion on Sony’s move to ditch physical disc releases.

"From a purely business perspective, I can understand why the people at Sony would make that decision.” said Niikawa, who was CEO of Nippon Ichi Software between 2009 to 2022. “However, the executives who decided it have probably never experienced coming to an event like Anime Expo and having someone approach them with a physical game to ask for an autograph. I don’t think they understand the feelings of those fans, and they may never have considered what physical editions mean to the people who value them."

Nikawa then added that "If they’re going to go as far as eliminating physical packages, they may as well eliminate the hardware too. A television would be enough. Why would you need the console? If you’re going to get rid of physical games, you may as well go all the way."

Sony’s digital game sales have been on the rise for years, far outselling physical releases. For example, just 7 PlayStation games have sold more than 100,000 physical copies in the US so far this year. Sony have framed their decision to stop releasing discs as following current PS4 and PS5 owners’ behavior. In the announcement on the official PlayStation blog, Sony framed phasing out discs as "a natural direction” for Sony as the company is adapting "to consumer trends as the general preference for digital media significantly outpaces physical discs."

Despite this trend, the backlash shows that physical media, especially the act of owning a game on a disc, is still very important to many. As Niikawa referenced, there is the importance of having something physical to put on your shelf. However, a disc-less box with a download code inside just doesn’t cut it for many, as shown by the backlash to GTA6’s physical release.

From conservationists’ point of view, games getting a disc release that only contains part of the game (see 007: First Light for a recent example) or which require a patch download to function properly has been a growing issue in both the PS4 and PS5 generations. This calls into question whether there is any value at all in having a physical game that can’t even be played without a download from a server.

Others in the Japanese game industry have also weighed in on Sony’s decision, with many raising concerns about the risks to game ownership and preservation in a digital-only future. Death Stranding creator Hideo Kojima expressed concern about how access to digital content can easily be withdrawn, removing the purchaser’s ability to own and use it when they wish. More recently, Kojima said of Sony’s decision that "I grew up with physical media, so I find it really sad." Nier creator Yoko Taro also echoed these sentiments in a recent tweet where he urged people to buy physical game releases while they still can.

Sony’s statements point clearly to games being digital only on the upcoming PS6, which is likely to be some kind of hybrid console/handheld, if comments from Sony CEO Nishino are anything to go by. It’s still unclear whether Sony will offer some kind of disc drive add-on that will enable gamers to play their discs from previous generations, or whether physical game collectors will just have to stick with older hardware.

Going forward, it seems that true physical games (where everything is actually in the box and ready to play) could become a niche, expensive product, only released in limited quantities by companies like Super Rare and Limited Run, who have a long track record of re-releasing physical games on various platforms.

This week, it was claimed that Sony knew its decision to kill PlayStation 5 discs would spark outrage, and reportedly has issued staff with the "strictest" social media guidelines to stop them from publicly commenting on the controversy.

Verity Townsend is a Japan-based freelance writer who previously served as editor, contributor and translator for the game news site Automaton West. She has also written about Japanese culture and movies for various publications.

items.title: 'She's Not in This Movie': Tom Holland Insists Jean Grey Won't Appear in Spider-Man: Brand New Day — So Is He Lying, or Is Sadie Sink Really Playing Someone Else?
items.description: With just a week to go until the launch of Spider-Man: Brand New Day, Tom Holland has stunned fans by stating that X-Men hero Jean Grey is "not in this movie" — despite months of rumors that this is who Sadie Sink is playing.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
With just a week to go until the launch of Spider-Man: Brand New Day, Tom Holland has stunned fans by stating that X-Men hero Jean Grey is "not in this movie" — despite months of rumors that this is who Sadie Sink is playing.

Brand New Day's buildup has been dominated by speculation over who Sink has been cast as, with an array of possible names initially in the mix. But, over time, insider whispers and fan discussion have coalesced around Jean Grey — to the point that if it now is anyone but her, many moviegoers would be floored.

Still, nothing is official. Which is why it's even more surprising that Holland has now responded to a comment about Jean Grey during a recent interview. Rather than decline to say anything further, the Spider-Man star instead took the opportunity to bluntly deny that the X-Men member would appear.

"Jean Grey can help her," stated Brazilian TikToker Natalia Kreuser, suggesting that the superhero's psychic powers could help recover MJ's lost memories of Peter Parker. "She's not in this movie but it would be pretty cool," Holland responded.

‘Oh she’s not in this movie, but that would be pretty cool’ - Tom Holland when asked if Jean Grey would help Peter Parker.

He says this while trying to hide a smile, cheeky 😉 😂 pic.twitter.com/KSkeuDhxnc

— SukunaOnFN (@SukunaOnFN1) July 23, 2026

Is Holland playing coy? There's seemingly no way to interpret his remark as anything other than a flat denial of Jean Grey being in the movie — which would, as we've said, be a big surprise at this point.

Or, is Holland now employing the Andrew Garfield trick of straight-up misdirecting fans? After months of being asked whether he was in Spider-Man: No Way Home, Garfield began flatly denying that — though, of course, he was indeed present.

Last year, it was reported that Sink will be back in 2027's climactic Multiverse Saga finale Avengers: Secret Wars, something that seemingly sets her up for a far bigger MCU role. Of course, Marvel is currently prepping its big X-Men reboot, which is being helmed by Thunderbolts/The New Avengers director Jake Schreier. Introducing Jean Grey now would allow Marvel to gently introduce audiences to the idea of a fresh generation of X-Men, before fans get to say farewell to various legacy characters who are returning for Avengers: Doomsday.

Speaking on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon, Sink discussed the huge amount of secrecy over her role and described not being able to say who she's playing as "torture." Subsequent trailers have kept Sink in the shadows, though she has now begun giving interviews on Spider-Man: Brand New Day's promotional tour, with rather amusingly tight-lipped results.

Beyond a marketing tactic to get fans speculating, director Destin Daniel Cretton has insisted that fans will ultimately appreciate being kept in suspense, and stated that Marvel was keeping the identity of Sadie Sink's character a secret until fans see the movie for a "very real reason" that he believes fans won't "get mad at."

Whatever the truth is, there's thankfully now just one week to go until we finally find out — as Spider-Man: Brand New Day opens in theaters on July 31.

Image credit: James McCauley/Variety via Getty Images

items.title: Scott Pilgrim Creator Bryan Lee O'Malley Returns to the Series for the First New Comic in 16 Years | Comic Con 2026
items.description: Oni Press has revealed that Scott Pilgrim creator Bryan Lee O'Malley is returning to the series for its first new comic in 16 years.
items.author: Jesse Schedeen
items.content:
Scott Pilgrim creator Bryan Lee O'Malley may have ended his beloved saga 16 years ago with the release of Scott Pilgrim's Finest Hour, but it seems he's still not quite done. Today at Comic-Con, Oni Press announced a new Scott Pilgrim comic called Scott Pilgrim EX: Dawn of Metal Scott.

As first revealed by Gizmodo, Scott Pilgrim EX: Dawn of Metal Scott is a one-shot prequel to the recently released beat-em-up game Scott Pilgrim EX (which also makes this a sequel to the animated series Scott Pilgrim Takes Off). Check out a short preview of the issue in the slideshow gallery below:

Here's the official description for Scott Pilgrim EX: Dawn of Metal Scott:

Scott met Ramona. Sparks flew. The two of them had to work together in order to defeat Ramona’s Seven Evil Exes and their nefarious leader, Gideon Gordon Graves. Some other stuff happened in various media formats that may or may not be canon. That’s all in the past. These days, Scott and Ramona are a happy couple, and the Exes have moved on from their unhealthy obsessions. I guess they all got therapy or whatever. Now, after a period of peace, a new threat is about to emerge. Are our heroes ready? Let’s find out!!!

“When I was asked to create a minicomic for Scott Pilgrim EX, I quickly said yes without considering the implications,” O’Malley said in a statement. “Only when I started writing and drawing it did I realize this would be the first new Scott Pilgrim comic in 16 years. items.title: Everything Announced at the Marvel's Wolverine: Deep Cuts SDCC Panel | Comic Con 2026
items.description: Our San Diego Comic-Con 2026 live reporting kicks off with Insomniac’s panel for upcoming PlayStation 5 exclusive, Marvel’s Wolverine. Here's everything that was announced.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
San Diego Comic-Con 2026 is here, and IGN is at the show reporting live on all the panels that matter.

Our live reporting kicked off with Insomniac’s panel for upcoming PlayStation 5 exclusive, Marvel’s Wolverine, direct from Hall H. There, Insomniac Games’ creative director Marcus Smith, game director Mike Daly, narrative director Walt Williams, and senior project director Jess Reiner-Reed, alongside actors Liam McIntyre (Wolverine) and Krizia Bajos (Jean Grey), as well as executive producer Eric Monacelli from Marvel Games, debuted a new trailer for the game, discussed its various characters, and announced a surprise crossover with fighting game Marvel's Wolverine X Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls.

You can catch up on all our live reporting below. And when you're done with that, be sure to check out our big interview with Insomniac Games from June, where we found out a lot more about how Marvel’s Wolverine works and plays, including information on co-op combat with Jean Grey.

Then, on Friday, July 24 and Saturday, July 25, IGN will stream live from San Diego with A-list interviews, exclusive reveals, and live coverage of SDCC’s biggest panels and announcements. Our broadcast runs from 3pm PT / 6pm ET to 7pm PT / 10pm ET each day and streams across IGN platforms. Here's our live show schedule.

Lightning round

The panel ended with some closing thoughts about Marvel's Wolverine. Marcus Smith said he hopes players feel powerful when they go hands-on. Jess Reiner-Reed is excited for players to see all the suits. Mike Daly namechecked Wolverine's Beserker Rage, where you "feel the frenzy." Eric Monacelli praised the "emotional depth and complexity in our cast of characters. These became my favorite versions of these characters." Liam McIntyre said playing Wolverine was the "biggest honor of my life. I hope you trust me with this character." And Krizia Bajos said she could wait for players to experience the game after working on it for four years.

Marvel's Wolverine X Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls

Game director Mike Daly says unlocking and crafting iconic suits for these characters is a part of the fun, and when Insomniac saw Wolverine in Arc System Works' fighting game Marvel Tokon, they wanted his look in their game. So, Insomniac created a suit inspired by the one Wolverine wears in Marvel Tokon. In Marvel's Wolverine, you unlock the Tokon suit by entering a Japanese arcade.

The crossover works both ways. Marvel's Wolverine's Battle Reborn suit is coming to Tokon on September 1.

Marvel’s Wolverine is getting a suit inspired by Marvel Tōkon Fighting Souls

Marvel Tōkon Fighting Souls is also getting a suit inspired by Marvel’s Wolverine#SDCC pic.twitter.com/Iyap6BxwH0

— IGN (@IGN) July 23, 2026

Marvel's Wolverine's soundtrack composer revealed

Award-winning composer David Fleming is at the helm of Marvel's Wolverine's soundtrack. You can listen to a track from the game later today. The full soundtrack releases August 28, 2026

Marvel's Wolverine prequel comic

Insomniac is now discussing the just-announced Marvel's Wolverine prequel comic. When you start the game you'll meet Logan who's been out of the game for some time. He quit and walked away without saying goodbye. The prequel will reveal more of that story, which sets up the game.

"Wolverine and the mutants of Team X are preparing to infiltrate Sentinel creator Bolivar Trask's secret base, and what they find within will tear them apart!" reads the official description. Part one is available online on Marvel Unlimited.

Marvel’s Wolverine is getting a prequel comic about how and why Logan left Team X, and it’s available at the Marvel booth at #SDCC pic.twitter.com/ZbSSSZle5o

— IGN (@IGN) July 23, 2026

The Hand

Wolverine also faces off against the demon-worshipping ninja cult, The Hand (who we will also see in this month's Spider-Man: Brand New Day). Senior project director Jess Reiner-Reed confirmed that Lady Deathstrike is the leader of The Hand in Marvel's Wolverine, and is a formidable foe for Logan. The Hand is connected to Logan in some way, and he will fight them throughout the game, eventually ending up in Japan.

We see Wolverine burst through a window, sword in his body, get up and shove the sword through a ninja. He can take that damage and get right back up, thanks to his Healing Factor.

Trask Industries

Trask Industries plays a big role in Marvel's Wolverine, posing a significant threat. Creative director Marcus Smith says "billionaires can cause damage. It turns out that having unlimited resources and a strong opinion can lead to some bad things." Trask sees mutants as a threat and will use his resources to eliminate them from the planet. To that end, Trask uses The Reavers, people cybernetically implanted with advanced technology.

Where are the X-Men?

While Marvel's Wolverine features Team X, the X-Men do not exist in the world of the game. Eric Monacelli from Marvel Games says this was a deliberate choice for Earth-1048, the universe that serves as the setting for various Marvel video games developed by Insomniac Games.

Instead, the game features Team X, a spec ops group that formed in the 1960s by Nathaniel Essex to fight the existential threat posed by Bolivar Trask. In the story, Logan left Team X three years ago under tense circumstances, leaving Essex feeling abandoned. Now, he's angry that he's returned.

As we knew, Mystique is in Marvel's Wolverine. Mutants in the game's world live in the shadows, so Team X allows her to be herself.

We know that the X-Men don’t exist in Marvel’s Wolverine, but Team X does, and it comprises of Sabertooth, Wolverine, and Mystique. #SDCC pic.twitter.com/ih9GIgjGRJ

— IGN (@IGN) July 23, 2026

What role does Jean Grey play in the story?

We're told Jean Grey has been out on her own, constantly on the move, discovering other people have powers (the X-Men do not exist in Marvel's Wolverine). Jean wants to give these other mutants what she didn't have, a place where they can be safe. That's how she crosses paths with this ruggedly handsome stranger (Wolverine), who she can't believe is willing to do so much to help the mutants.

Krizia Bajos, who plays Jean Grey, says that when she meets Logan, "there's something there, a cosmic connection. She can see through his walls and his wounds."

Who is Insomniac's Wolverine?

Mike Daly says this is Insomniac's take on the Wolverine we all know. "We set out to create the ultimate Wolverine game and that meant bringing to life all the traits that make this character beloved. He's cynical, candid he keeps people at a distance. He has a big heart.

"We prioritized claw combat, that was an essential part of the character. Leveraging his mutant healing factor, deep rage, enhanced senses to track and scout enemies to sense incoming danger and feel his heavy skeleton as you push forward. We wanted to make sure his personality came through in eshc action.. His lost memories, you will be peeling back layers of his past. Not an origin story, same universe as marvel spider man games!

"When we bring all those things together, it's all directed toward delivering a singular feeling to the player. I feel like Wolverine!"

McIntyre, who plays Wolverine, thanks Insomniac for trusting him to play the much-loved X-Men character. He says he found Wolverine via the X-Men animated series and "I've loved it ever since."

New Wolverine trailer

We have a new Marvel's Wolverine trailer, which just debuted during the SDCC panel. This one focuses on the story, and sets up Jean Grey as a potential love interest for Logan. We also see a number of already revealed characters, including Sabretooth and Lady Deathstrike. It looks like part of the story will revolve around Wolverine recovering his memory of past exploits, as well as saving mutants from harm.

Here we go!

Not long now...

15 minutes to go! We're almost ready for the Marvel's Wolverine panel to begin. Keep an eye out for updates right here.

The countdown begins...

We have just one hour to go before Insomaniac's Marvel's Wolverine panel begins. We'll be in Hall H bringing you all the news as it happens. Stay tuned!

Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

items.title: Microsoft Launches Test for Ad-Supported Xbox Game Streaming, Promises the Ads Will Not 'Interrupt the Flow of Gameplay'
items.description: Ad-supported Xbox game streaming is here, Microsoft has said. Here's how it works and how you can try it out.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Microsoft has launched a test for ad-supported Xbox game streaming, and promised the ads won't interrupt gameplay.

The test lets users stream select games from their library for a limited time supported by adverts, and is available to Xbox Insiders. During this test period, Xbox Insiders with an Xbox account can stream supported games without a subscription for free with ads, with one-hour session limits across supported devices and regions where game streaming is available.

Ads will play before streaming sessions begin and will not interrupt gameplay, Microsoft insisted. The core game experience remains unchanged, the company added. Participation is optional, and players can choose other ways to play at any time.

The test is designed to help give more people more affordable ways to play on devices they already own, Microsoft explained. You can play after sitting through two minutes of ads. When your 1-hour session ends, you can play again after sitting through another set of ads, and your progress continues across your account and devices. It's also worth noting that today, Xbox Cloud Gaming is not available without a Game Pass subscription.

“For many players, the device they already own now allows them to stream games with Xbox,” Microsoft said. “Cloud can also help Xbox One owners play newer games built for Xbox Series X|S without needing to purchase new hardware right away. That can be especially meaningful in places where consoles are harder to find or less affordable, giving more players another way to access great games on devices they already have.

“Advertising has existed in gaming for decades, from in-game placements to free-to-play models. But it hasn’t always been built with the player in mind. When done well, advertising can help lower the cost of access. It creates another way for players to get into games without an upfront streaming purchase and expands audiences through new ways to play.

“For brands, this only works if showing up here adds to the experience, not takes away from it.”

In a blog post on Xbox Wire, Microsoft outlined the following guidelines for ad-supported game streaming:

  1. We start with the player. Ads should create value.
  2. We do not interrupt the flow of gameplay.
  3. We hold ads to the same quality bar as our content.
  4. We’re clear about what’s advertising.
  5. We make sure ads fit what players expect on each platform.

Microsoft said it will learn from the test and improve it based on feedback.

The test of ad-supported Xbox game streaming arrives amid console price rises that are pushing some gaming hardware towards the $1,000 mark. Last month, Microsoft announced significant price rises for Xbox consoles, blaming the ongoing “components crisis.” In a blog post, Microsoft said that from August 1, the price of Xbox consoles will increase by $100 for 512GB models, and $150 for 1TB models. The 2TB model will be discontinued.

Xbox console price rises June 2026:

  • Xbox Series S 512GB: $399.99 —> $499.99
  • Xbox Series S 1TB: $449.99 —> $599.99
  • Xbox Series X 1TB Digital: $599.99 —> $749.99
  • Xbox Series X 1TB: $649.99 —> $799.99

“Last October, we increased Xbox console price by $20-$70 in the U.S.” Microsoft said at the time. “We hoped another price increase would not be necessary, and we have spent the last several months working with suppliers on options. Unfortunately, console storage and memory prices have increased by more than 2.5x and we expect another doubling by the fall of 2027.

"The entire consumer electronics industry is struggling with the current components crisis, but the effects are particularly hard on consoles. Unlike phones, computers, speakers, and other consumer devices, consoles are typically not sold at a profit, but instead for less than they cost to make.”

New Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has said the spiralling cost of new and existing consoles would require "radically different business models" over the coming generation. She added that the industry had "reached a point where it will be hard to imagine" mass audiences still being able to afford "thousands of dollars" for a new console generation.

The current PS5 and Xbox Series X and S generation of consoles have seen price increases rather than cost savings. Sony itself raised the price of PS5 consoles back in March, blaming “continued pressures in the global economic landscape.” Nintendo has also not been immune, and recently acknowledged it would up the price of Switch 2, just over a year after its arrival. And Valve has bemoaned its struggle to release Steam Machine at the price it had initially hoped, instead having to go for an eye-watering $1,049.

With this context, it's easy to see why Microsoft would want to introduce ad-supported Xbox game streaming now. I imagine Sharma also has an eye on the response to the test ahead of any potential introduction of ad-supported gaming on the non-streaming side.

The test also comes amid what Sharma has called the most significant restructure in Xbox history. 1,600 staff were cut from Microsoft’s gaming business earlier this month, with another 1,600 to go over the current financial year. Four studios have left the business, with another on the way out.

“Our business today is not healthy,” Sharma said. “We are operating at margins that are 3-10x lower than comparable platform and publishing businesses. We entered Gen 9 with a smaller install base and a higher cost structure. To grow, we bet on Game Pass, multi-platform, and a broader portfolio of content. While those businesses have created meaningful value, they did not grow at the pace we expected. As that happened, our core business weakened, and we added more teams, more investment, and more time, hoping for a better outcome. And now the industry is facing the most severe hardware crisis in its history. We must reset Xbox.”

Yesterday, Microsoft announced Xbox Backward Compatibility on PC, allowing you to play classic console games on PC and handhelds such as the Xbox Ally X for the first time.

Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

With this context, it's easy to see why Microsoft would want to introduce ad-supported Xbox game streaming now. I imagine Sharma also has an eye on the response to the test ahead of any potential introduction of ad-supported gaming on the non-streaming side.

The test also comes amid what Sharma has called the most significant restructure in Xbox history. 1,600 staff were cut from Microsoft’s gaming business earlier this month, with another 1,600 to go over the current financial year. Four studios have left the business, with another on the way out.

“Our business today is not healthy,” Sharma said. “We are operating at margins that are 3-10x lower than comparable platform and publishing businesses. We entered Gen 9 with a smaller install base and a higher cost structure. To grow, we bet on Game Pass, multi-platform, and a broader portfolio of content. While those businesses have created meaningful value, they did not grow at the pace we expected. As that happened, our core business weakened, and we added more teams, more investment, and more time, hoping for a better outcome. And now the industry is facing the most severe hardware crisis in its history. We must reset Xbox.”

Yesterday, Microsoft announced Xbox Backward Compatibility on PC, allowing you to play classic console games on PC and handhelds such as the Xbox Ally X for the first time.

items.title: Former Assassin's Creed, Watch Dogs Director Likens Large-Scale Game Development to Working With 'Flaming Barrels Falling Down From a Construction Site,' Months After Parting Ways With Ubisoft
items.description: Watch Dogs and Splinter Cell veteran Clint Hocking has described the experience of leading a large team within Ubisoft as like working while "flaming barrels [are] falling down from a construction site," akin to a scene from Donkey Kong.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Watch Dogs and Splinter Cell development veteran Clint Hocking has described the experience of leading a large team within Ubisoft as like working while "flaming barrels [are] falling down from a construction site," akin to a scene from the arcade game Donkey Kong.

Hocking made the comment as part of a lengthy discussion about how his role changed as development team sizes grew, leading him to feel less effective while leading Ubisoft's multi-studio effort on Watch Dogs Legion.

Hocking and Ubisoft parted ways abruptly earlier this year amid a reshuffle at the top of the publisher's prized Assassin's Creed brand, despite being in the middle of leading development on Assassin's Creed Hexe. The franchise's next blockbuster, Hexe is understood to still be on target to arrive in 2027.

"On [Splinter Cell] Chaos Theory, I would just walk over to the desk of the person who was making a thing, and sit down with them and talk to them about what they're doing," Hocking recalled, speaking via the FRVR podcast.

"We could have a conversation," he continued, suggesting a scenario where he was able to offer granular input such as the placement of a specific light source to better guide player movement.

"But on a huge game with 1,000 people, you go into a meeting to review some piece of content — some quest, say, or some location — and there's 30 people in the meeting," Hocking continued. "Directors and producers and project managers, and very often even the level designer who built it isn't even in the meeting.

"And it's like, 'where's the person who worked on this?' 'Ah, they're working on the thing they need to do for their next meeting. But don't worry we'll take notes and put it in Jira for them.' So there's people there writing down what you say, making tasks of it.

"Then you finish the review, you say, 'OK, when are we going to see the iterations and the improvements we talked about?' And they're like, 'Well... so it's going to be six weeks before we see an iteration on this because the person who needs to do the iteration is working on this [other thing].' Then, by the time you get back there six weeks later, maybe the whole context is different. It very often feels like... you know those flaming barrels that Donkey Kong throws down at you? Very often game development feels like this stream of burning barrels falling down from a construction site."

Hocking initially joined Ubisoft to work on the legendary 2002 stealth action adventure Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell, which he contributed to as a designer and scriptwriter. Hocking then served as creative director on its follow-up, Splinter Cell: Chaos Theory, before holding the same role on Far Cry 2.

During a period away from Ubisoft, Hocking served years at LucasArts, Valve, and Amazon. Hocking then returned to Ubisoft to serve once again as a creative director, this time on Watch Dogs: Legion, which launched in 2020 to a mixed response. Following that, Hocking moved over to Assassin's Creed, and had been leading work on Hexe out of the company's Montreal studio. Legion remains Hocking's only shipped title since Far Cry 2 back in 2008.

Hocking's role leading Assassin's Creed Hexe has now been taken up by Jean Guesdon, the Assassin's Creed franchise's Head of Content, who is seen as a steady and experience hand with a lengthy track record working on numerous titles in the series.

Photo by ROBYN BECK/AFP via Getty Images.
